column2: Why is impairment alone an insufficient scientific target for rehabilitation medicine?
column3: Function and disability arise from disease, injury, environment and personal factors interacting, so the target also includes activity, participation, adaptation and quality of life.

column3: The environment shapes the consequences of impairment: inaccessible transport can magnify a modest impairment, while support and technology can permit participation despite severe impairment.

column3: The medical model identifies pathology and treatment and the social model identifies barriers, discrimination and exclusion, so clinicians treat remediable disease while changing environments that unnecessarily disable.

column3: Function is task- and context-specific, so it does not show ability to cross a road, climb home stairs or sustain work; assessment asks what the person needs to do, under what conditions and at what cost.
